newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB end down, sales spurred by news item on budget.
newsitem.headline: JGB end down, sales spurred by news item on budget.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures ended sharply lower on Wednesday as selling was triggered by a local news agency report which appeared late in the afternoon.

A senior member of the Liberal Democratic Party, Taku Yamazaki, said a supplementary budget worth about five trillion yen must be considered at a special parliamentary session after general elections on October 20, Jiji news agency reported.
The December ended at 122.62, down sharply from Tuesday's 122.95.
The key futures contract moved within a range of 122.60 to 123.07 during the day.

"The news report about the supplementary budget caused a round of selling," said a trader for a trust bank's securities unit. The downward momentum increased when the December fell below the previous day's low of 122.79, the trader said.

A rumour about a fund set up as part of a government scheme to wind up failed mortgage firms and its investment strategy was also a sell factor, said another trader for a trust bank's securities affiliate.

There was a rumour that the new Financial Stabilisation Fund, worth about 800 billion yen excluding a 100 billion yen contribution from the Bank of Japan, would invest in short-term instruments for the time being, the second trader said.

Talk that city banks were selling cash bond brands near the 182nd benchmark and that life insurers were selling brands near the 140th JGB may have forced traders with long positions to unwind their positions, the first trader said.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd cash JGB stood at 2.830 percent as of 0704 GMT, up from Tuesday's 2.790 percent.
Before the December's sudden fall late in the afternoon, many market players had been taking a wait-and-see stance ahead of the general elections on October 20, traders said.
Traders said they would also be keeping a close eye on a 10-year JGB auction expected next Tuesday, and a BOJ branch managers' meeting which will start next Monday.
The coupon rate for the 10-year JGBs to be offered in the auction is likely to be set somewhere between 2.8 percent and 3.0 percent, traders said.
There would be little demand for the new cash JGBs if the coupon rate was set at 2.8 percent, a city bank trader said.
The second trader said he felt a coupon rate of 2.8 percent was unlikely under current market conditions, but that even a 2.9 percent coupon rate might not invite much demand.
The BOJ branch managers' meeting is unlikely to lead to a rise in interest rates, a trust bank trader said.
"I doubt that there will be any talk of raising interest rates at the meeting," the trader said.
